researcher_a.name: Dr. Amara Chen
researcher_a.bio: Works on low-resource NLP, multilingual models, and data-efficient learning.

researcher_b.name: Prof. Elena Petrova
researcher_b.bio: Speech recognition for under-resourced languages and speech accessibility.

source_papers.title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of Multilingual Language Models for Low-Resource Languages
source_papers.abstract: Multilingual language models often underperform on low-resource languages due to limited training data. We propose a data-efficient adaptation strategy combining cross-lingual transfer with lightweight parameter tuning. Experiments across eight low-resource languages show consistent gains over strong baselines while using only a fraction of labeled data. Limitations include reliance on a related high-resource pivot language and evaluation restricted to text classification.

source_papers.title: Few-Shot Named Entity Transfer with Synthetic Corpus Augmentation
source_papers.abstract: We study few-shot named entity recognition when almost no target-language annotations exist. A synthetic corpus augmentation pipeline generates pseudo-labeled examples from a related language. The method improves F1 by 6 points in the few-shot setting. Future work includes extending to structured prediction tasks beyond sequence labeling and reducing dependence on hand-built lexicons.

source_papers.title: Active Annotation Selection for Under-Resourced Text Analytics
source_papers.abstract: Annotation budgets dominate the cost of building NLP systems for under-resourced languages. We introduce an active annotation selection framework that combines uncertainty sampling with diversity constraints. Across three tasks the approach reaches baseline quality with 40% fewer labels. A key limitation is the assumption of a stable annotation interface, which may not hold in practice.

source_papers.title: Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Under-Resourced Languages
source_papers.abstract: Self-supervised speech models transfer poorly to very low-resource languages. We fine-tune with language-adaptive pretraining on unlabeled radio archives, cutting word error rate by 18% on two languages. Compute cost of adaptation is high, motivating parameter-efficient adaptation as future work.

source_papers.title: Accessible Voice Interfaces: Error Patterns for Dysarthric Speech
source_papers.abstract: We analyze recognition error patterns for dysarthric speech across commercial and research systems. A taxonomy of errors shows systematic confusions linked to prosodic patterns rather than articulation alone. Dataset diversity is limited and largely English-centric, which constrains generalization claims.

expected_gaps.description: Data-efficient transfer methods are validated mostly for text; under-resourced speech lacks comparable lightweight parameter-efficient adaptation baselines.
Synthetic data augmentation is rarely evaluated jointly across text and speech within one data-efficiency framework.

researcher_a.bio: Epidemic forecasting, spatiotemporal modeling, public health informatics.

researcher_b.name: Dr. Priya Raghavan
researcher_b.bio: Deep learning for medical image segmentation and clinical deployment.

cases.field_query: healthcare analytics and clinical decision support

source_papers.title: Bayesian Hierarchical Models for Epidemic Nowcasting with Mobility Data
source_papers.abstract: Timely epidemic nowcasting benefits from mobility signals. We develop a Bayesian hierarchical model fusing case reports with mobility indices, improving short-horizon forecasts in two synthetic districts. Mobility biases across demographic groups are not fully corrected, and equity implications require dedicated study.

source_papers.title: Spatiotemporal Graph Models for Disease Spread Prediction
source_papers.abstract: We model disease spread with spatiotemporal graphs whose edges encode human mobility. The model predicts district-level incidence with lower error than purely temporal baselines across simulated outbreaks. Robustness to reporting delays and sparse surveillance is identified as a key limitation.

source_papers.title: Self-Supervised Pretraining for Medical Image Segmentation with Scarce Labels
source_papers.abstract: Labeled medical images are scarce and expensive. We study self-supervised pretraining strategies for segmentation under label scarcity, comparing contrastive and masked-image objectives. Pretraining improves Dice scores by up to 5 points on two modalities. Gains shrink for out-of-distribution scanners, motivating domain-general pretraining as future work.

source_papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Segmentation for Clinical Decision Support
source_papers.abstract: Clinical adoption of deep segmentation requires trustworthy uncertainty estimates. We propose an uncertainty-aware segmentation network with calibration losses and evaluate clinician trust in a reader study. Calibration improves without sacrificing accuracy. The study size is small, and workflow integration in busy clinics remains untested.

expected_gaps.description: Uncertainty quantification in clinical segmentation rarely exploits spatiotemporal or Bayesian modeling from epidemic forecasting.
Self-supervised pretraining for segmentation has not been evaluated under the active-labeling constraints typical of clinical deployment.
